newsitem.title: ITALY: Indictments sought in Venice lagoon pollution case.
newsitem.headline: Indictments sought in Venice lagoon pollution case.

text.p: Venice's public prosecutor on Thursday sought the indictments of 25 former chemical company executives on charges relating to pollution of the north-eastern city's lagoon.

Prosecutor Felice Casson said he had asked an examining judge to order trials for ex-directors of Montedison, Enichem and the defunct Enimont venture which operate, or operated in the past, the Porto Marghera industrial complex on the mainland shore of Venice's lagoon.

The specific charges were not revealed, but Casson said the case related to an investigation to determine who was responsible for the discharge of chemical products into the lagoon from the Porto Marghera complex.
The examining judge will hold a hearing on March 3 before ruling on Casson's request.
Independent scientists and the environmental group Greenpeace confirmed in August that toxic dioxins were present in the lagoon, including the famed Grand Canal.
They said high levels of dioxins were found around the Porto Marghera complex and lower levels in other areas of the lagoon.
Dioxins are found in weedkillers and bleaching agents. They can cause cancer, liver and kidney diseases and birth defects.
